Agorapulse vs VEXI: How They Compare in 2026
Agorapulse and VEXI, side by side: what each one does and what it costs, from each company's own pages.
Compare Agorapulse vs VEXI side-by-side. See pricing, features, and why 1,000+ realtors choose VEXI for done-for-you social media.

Agorapulse is a social media platform for teams to publish, answer comments and messages, listen and report on results [1]. VEXI makes and posts your social content. They overlap on scheduling, and in many ways they fit together.

Agorapulse calls itself the AI social media platform built for business results: your team plans, publishes, answers comments and messages in one inbox, listens for mentions and reports on results and ROI [1]. Its AI Writing Assistant crafts captions and post text, and Archie, its AI content repurposing tool, turns webinars, articles, documents and videos into platform-native posts, branded images and short clips [2][3]. Plans are priced per user: Standard is $79, Professional $119 and Advanced $149 a user a month billed annually, or $99, $149 and $199 paying monthly, and Custom is priced on request [2]. You can try it free for 30 days with no credit card [2].

VEXI (formerly Social Realtr) is an AI content studio that runs social media for entrepreneurs and creators. You describe what you want and it makes the posts, videos, designs and captions, then schedules and publishes them. Plans start at $199 a month, and every plan starts with a 15-day trial.
The two overlap on scheduling and posting and do different main jobs. Here is what each one does.

Agorapulse’s AI Writing Assistant creates on-brand captions and post text and suggests hashtags and alt text, and Archie turns your webinars, articles and videos into platform-native posts, branded images, carousels and short clips that you review, edit and schedule [1][3][4].
VEXI does it all for you.
Archie turns long videos into Reels or short clips with captions, and you schedule them to your calendar from the Agorapulse composer [3].
VEXI edits your videos for you.

Agorapulse gathers comments, DMs and reviews from all your networks in one inbox, with AI reply suggestions and sentiment, and its reports cover post performance, your team’s replies and the ROI of your posts [1][2].

Agorapulse is priced per user, from $79 a user a month billed annually or $99 paying monthly on Standard; Standard, Professional and Advanced each include 10 social profiles, and you can add more [2].

A fit for teams and agencies who want one place to publish, answer comments and messages, listen for mentions and report on results, with AI for captions and Archie to turn long content into posts and clips [1][3][4].
Built for people who want it done right.
Does Agorapulse create content for you?

Its AI helps with the drafts [3][4]. Agorapulse’s AI Writing Assistant improves your copy or starts from a prompt, and suggests hashtags and alt text [4]. Archie turns your webinars, articles, documents, podcasts and videos into platform-native posts, branded images and short clips that you review, edit and schedule; it is free to use right now [3].
What does Agorapulse do with video?

Agorapulse’s Archie turns long videos into Reels or short clips with captions, and you schedule them from the Agorapulse composer [3]. On Professional and up you can also upload .srt subtitle files to scheduled video posts [2].
Which networks does Agorapulse work with?

Agorapulse connects Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, X (Twitter), YouTube, Threads, Pinterest, Bluesky and Google Business profiles, and lets you schedule as many posts as you want across them [2].

Agorapulse is priced per user: Standard is $79, Professional $119 and Advanced $149 a user a month billed annually, or $99, $149 and $199 paying monthly; Custom is priced on request [2]. You can try it free for 30 days with no credit card, and after the trial you can pick a paid plan or keep using the free plan [2].

Agorapulse’s plans run from Standard, built for social media managers handling it all themselves, to Custom, for large teams or enterprises [2]. It has solution pages for agencies, e-commerce, B2B enterprises, manufacturing, retail and higher education [1].
Two different main jobs, with some overlap.
